item.title: Why not to bank on Trump's $5,000 dividend checks happening
item.description: President Trump pledged $5,000 checks to all American adults if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate. You may not be able to take that to the bank.

item.title: Rolling over a 401(k) to gold? What to check before you move your money
item.description: A gold rollover can reshape your retirement portfolio, making it important to know what you're signing up for.

item.title: A 9/11 memorial is unfinished and in disrepair. A first responder is pushing for its restoration.
item.description: Advocates for New Jersey's "Empty Sky" 9/11 memorial say the monument has fallen into disrepair and needs to be completed. First responder Kathe Conlon explains why the memorial matters and remembers her team's rescue efforts after the September 11, 2001, attacks.

item.title: Is $10,000 in credit card debt enough for debt forgiveness?
item.description: A five-figure credit card balance can be tough to tackle, but does it make debt forgiveness a realistic option?

item.title: Iran strikes U.S. jets after Trump promises war to end after midterms
item.description: U.S. jets were hit by Iranian missiles while parked at a base in Jordan, sources tell CBS News, while Trump said the war will end "immediately" after midterms.

item.title: Daughters of 9/11 victims seek answers about accused mastermind's trial
item.description: A new documentary, "Daughters of 9/11," follows their pursuit of information and closure, which they were determined to find for themselves, other families who lost loved ones in the attacks and the American public.

item.title: George W. Bush says Americans "don't pay attention to the lesson of 9/11"
item.description: Former President George W. Bush gave rare remarks on Wednesday as Americans mark 25 years since the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks.

item.title: First-ever adult T. rex trackway found in North Dakota
item.description: Paleontologists have identified the first known trackway made by a full-grown Tyrannosaurus rex, and the discovery was made in the North Dakota badlands.

item.title: Trump touts "great conversation" with Putin on ending the war in Ukraine
item.description: Russian attacks continue to ravage Ukraine. President Trump says he spoke with President Vladimir Putin about ending the war. Plus, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's plane was nearly struck by a Russian drone, according to Norway's prime minister. CBS News' Aidan Stretch reports.

item.title: What will victory look like in Iran? "60 Minutes" asks Hegseth
item.description: President Trump says the Iran war will not end before the midterm elections conclude. CBS News' Norah O'Donnell asked Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth about the conflict for "60 Minutes."

item.title: Daughters of 9/11 victims on their journeys to seek justice
item.description: A new Paramount+ documentary "Daughters of 9/11" digs into the investigation into the alleged mastermind of the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks, Khalid Sheikh Mohammed. Two women who lost their fathers in the tragedy, Elizabeth Miller and Jessica Trant, join "CBS Mornings," along with former FBI special agent Frank Pellegrino to talk about 25 years since the terror attacks.

item.title: Oil hovers above $100 a barrel as Iran war worries rise
item.description: Oil prices continue to climb as the U.S. and Iran trade strikes. CBS News' Kelly O'Grady reports on the key inflation indicators expected next.

item.title: Supreme Court blocks Missouri from using new map favoring GOP in fall elections
item.description: The Supreme Court said Missouri must use a 2022 congressional map — not a new congressional map that favors Republicans — in the 2026 midterm elections.

item.title: Gold Star parents demand details on Iranian strike that killed their son in Kuwait
item.description: Jim and Stacey Khork lost their son, U.S. Army Reserve Capt. Cody Khork, after he and five other U.S. troops were killed by an Iranian drone strike at a base in Kuwait. Now, the Khorks are asking the Army to release an internal investigation into the attack. CBS News' Jonah Kaplan reports.

item.title: Drake Maye throws 3 interceptions in 4th quarter of season opener
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks stunned the New England Patriots 13-10 in the NFL season opener Wednesday night after Drake Maye threw three interceptions during the fourth quarter. Nate Burleson has more.

item.title: Can you lower your credit card interest rate without hurting your credit score?
item.description: Cutting your credit card rate could save you money on interest, but some strategies come with a credit tradeoff.

item.title: Sandra Bullock on how motherhood and personal loss influenced her "Practical Magic 2" performance
item.description: Sandra Bullock and Lee Pace sat down with Adriana Diaz to discuss "Practical Magic 2," which premieres Friday.

item.title: Trump vows soaring oil prices will tumble after midterms
item.description: Oil prices are up as the war in Iran intensifies. President Trump promised lower gas prices for Americans after the midterm elections. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi reports.

item.title: The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was just the beginning, experts say
item.description: "What happens inside frontier AI companies now clearly affects everyone outside of them," an expert said following the hack on Hugging Face by AI agents being tested by OpenAI.

item.title: "48 Hours" show schedule
item.description: "48 Hours"' uncovers the narrative behind true crime cases with unmatched reporting and suspense.

item.title: Stella Parton says her sister Dolly was prepared and at peace when she died
item.description: Stella Parton gives insight into her sister Dolly Parton's marriage, makeup habits and views on death in an exclusive CBS News interview.

item.title: Multiple U.S. military aircraft damaged in Iranian strikes on base in Jordan, sources say
item.description: One A-10 Thunderbolt, an attack aircraft known as the Warthog, was struck and lost a wing, according to sources.

item.title: Prosecutor who withdrew from dismissed Adani bribery case fired, sources say
item.description: Andrew Tyler, who worked in the fraud section of the Criminal Division of DOJ, was removed Tuesday over allegations of ethical violations, sources said.

item.title: Stella Parton says sister Dolly Parton was "definitely prepared" and at peace when she died
item.description: Dolly Parton's sister, Stella, sits down with Gayle King for her first interview since Dolly's death to discuss her sister's legendary life. Stella Parton says the country star was "definitely prepared" and at peace when she died last month.

item.title: 25 people killed in fire on cargo ship docked in China, state media reports
item.description: The deadly fire broke out when the cargo ship was docked for repairs at a major shipping hub on China's northeastern coast.

item.title: Trump's Republican midterm convention included $5,000 pitch and Iran war expectations
item.description: President Trump headlined the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, Texas, promising Americans $5,000 "dividends" if his party takes the midterms. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: Parents of soldier killed by Iranian strike in Kuwait ask Army to investigate attack
item.description: Army Reserve Capt. Cody Khork was one of six U.S. troops killed in an Iranian drone strike on an Army base in Kuwait. His parents are now speaking out about their fight to get the Army to release details on an internal investigation. CBS News' Jonah Kaplan reports.

item.title: Lawsuit seeks to block deployment of ICE, federal agents to polling sites
item.description: A coalition of advocacy groups and a Democratic-led city filed a preemptive lawsuit seeking to block the Trump administration from deploying armed ICE agents to polling sites ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: Gold Star family calls on Army to release probe of deadly attack on Kuwait base
item.description: Six Americans were killed in the March 1 strike on a tactical operations center in Kuwait.

item.title: Barry Melrose, prominent NHL player, coach and broadcaster, dies at 70
item.description: Barry Melrose, a hockey player-turned-coach who led the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final before going on to a long career in broadcasting the sport, has died at 70.
